purpose: Rows seen on the official schedule page that fall OUTSIDE the 3-day pick window. Held separately so the pick slate cannot be silently widened, and so scheduling anomalies are recorded rather than explained away.
anomalies_note: The two consecutive-day repeat matchups below were transcribed exactly as rendered by the official schedule page. They are NOT used by any model output. Either the schedule genuinely repeats a pairing at the same arena on back-to-back nights, or the page rendered a duplicate card; the difference matters for any automated ingest, so it is flagged for a human with the site open.

records.observation: Identical matchup and arena (Scotiabank Arena) as 0022600241 on 2026-11-15, two days apart. Both were read from the same official schedule page.
Identical matchup and arena (Target Center) as 0022600250 on 2026-11-16, on consecutive days. Not a normal NBA scheduling pattern; recorded as a data-integrity flag.

Game IDs are not monotonic with date: Nov 13 runs 0022600034-0022600042 (Emirates NBA Cup group play) and Nov 14 resumes at 0022600231. Any pipeline that infers an ID from sequence will join the wrong game.

https://www.nba.com/games?dates=MM/DD/YYYY ignores the dates parameter for non-browser clients and always returns the current day's slate; the day picker is applied client-side. Date-window scrapes must use /schedule, not /games?dates=.
